result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.compose_all()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Combine any number of graphs with compose(). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.compose_all()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Combine any number of graphs with compose(). title: >- [Graph.compose_all()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Combine any number of graphs with compose(). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Combine any number of graphs with `compose()`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40453-L40496){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.compose_all(graphs) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Compose many graphs](../assets/graphs/compose-all.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three graphs on the same nodes A, B, C: base has edge A–B (accent), update1 adds B–C (teal), and update2 adds C–A (violet). compose_all merges nodes and edges by id from left to right, later graphs winning any attribute clash, so the result is the triangle A, B, C with 3 edges, each in the color of the graph that supplied it." width="100%"} Applies `compose()` from left to right, so nodes and edges are merged by ID and, where graphs disagree on attributes, later graphs win. Use it to overlay a series of updates on a base graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [graphs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A non-empty list of graphs with the same directedness. None is modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph (a copy, if only one graph is given). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the list is empty or the graphs differ in directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Equivalent to `graphs[0].compose(graphs[1]).compose(graphs[2])...`. Mirrors NetworkX's `compose_all`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#50fb5b26 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec base = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]).add_edge("A", "B") update1 = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]).add_edge("B", "C") update2 = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]).add_edge("C", "A") ec.Graph.compose_all([base, update1, update2]).count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
